label: SECOND MODEL FAMILY: GPT (Codex2)

step_checks.derivation: A catalogue of tested bound structures does not exclude untested larger bound states. Pair size two is a proposed operational definition, not a derivation of all possible small bound pieces. Admission followed by Bind can erase a written record unless extra conditions prevent it.

Each added edge has one new endpoint, so forward Birth never joins two existing vertices. The two siblings have no edge at creation. This proves non-adjacency for the no-undo growth protocol. General reverse reconnections need separate treatment; my limited two-Birth exact search found no counterexample among 48 candidates and proves no general extension.

With all endpoints written and a cut-lock on every written-written edge, every four-edge cut intersects locks, so no Birth is allowed. If a lock instead forbids only link-bit shifts/ring flips, it imposes no such cut restriction. These are distinct rule readings.

step_checks.grade: Conditional rare-pair mechanism confirmed analytically, thresholds not re-simulated
step_checks.derivation: If age density is lambda exp(-lambda a) and writes at the two newborns are independent rate w, then P(both)=1-2lambda/(lambda+w)+lambda/(lambda+2w), P(either)=1-lambda/(lambda+2w), P(heir)=w/(lambda+w). At w/lambda=.1 these are .01515,.16667,.09091. Thus changing the record predicate changes the rare-pair population by over tenfold; finite pieces under one predicate cannot establish PD-33 under another. Independent age assumptions are explicit.

step_checks.derivation: Mean-square displacement of concatenated runs includes 2 sum_{i<j}<Delta x_i dot Delta x_j>. Dropping those correlations precludes a rigorous upper bound from run lengths alone. No computed wave speed means no verified total crossover bound. 1.05/.76=1.38158 is only proxy arithmetic.
No global three-dimensional limit is established by finite ball and walk slopes. Supplied three-dimensional blocks remain inputs. Independent whole-body walk test follows in X3.

recomputed_numbers.note: No counterexample was found in the limited reverse-pairing search. The stored scope describes the attempted witness conditions, not an observed witness; witness is null.

disagreements_with_first_check: No contradiction to the first-check corrections. Narrow S3's forever language to the forward-only histories actually proved; no contrary full-rule theorem established.
Full lock-percolation and ring-dynamics simulations not re-executed; their sample thresholds remain first-family finite evidence.
corrections: Retain first-check downgrades of S1 and S4.
Do not equate pair record formation, both sites written, heir written, and permanent binding.
Keep supplied-block gamma estimate separate from unknown wave response and total crossover.
plain_summary: The first check's main downgrades are supported. Locking every written link blocks growth only when locks forbid cutting links. Whether one or both newborns must be written changes the estimated bound-pair population sharply: at a write-to-growth ratio of 0.1, the simple age model gives 16.7% versus 1.5%. That makes the lock definition and growth supply consequential. Short-ring snapshots do not establish permanent freezing, and the gamma estimate is not a proven bound on the light crossover. No board grade is upgraded.
